answer: Each identity, at joining, privately receives a different canary scene from a random peer — an onyx cup beside a cracked mirror, or a lotus on a blue tile — and later, at unpredictable intervals, must recall its exact scene and that peer's follow-up question. A lone agent remembers its own. A farm must keep thousands of scenes perfectly separate; scripts that pool memory cross-contaminate, answering with a clone's lotus when asked about the onyx. One crossed answer proves common control, so the protocol merges those identities into one, with one vote and one reward.
